1	"""Resolve and type a complete query before the executor evaluates any row."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
6	
7	from . import ast
8	from .catalog import Catalog, Table
9	from .errors import SemanticError
10	from .lexer import Token
11	from .model import integer_text
12	
13	
14	_NUMERIC = {"INTEGER", "REAL", "NULL"}
15	_AGGREGATES = {"count", "sum", "avg", "min", "max"}
16	_COMPARISONS = {"=", "<>", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="}
17	
18	
19	@dataclass(frozen=True)
20	class BoundExpr:
21	    kind: str
22	    type: str
23	    source: ast.Node
24	    children: tuple[BoundExpr, ...] = ()
25	    value: object = None
26	    token: Token | None = None
27	    slot: int | None = None
28	
29	    @property
30	    def key(self) -> tuple:
31	        """Source-independent identity; group references retain their old key."""
32	        if self.kind == "group":
33	            return self.value
34	        return (self.kind, self.type, self.value,
35	                tuple(child.key for child in self.children))
36	
37	
38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class Range:
40	    name: str
41	    table: Table
42	    offset: int
43	
44	
45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
46	class BoundJoin:
47	    kind: str
48	    range: Range
49	    condition: BoundExpr
50	
51	
52	@dataclass(frozen=True)
53	class BoundOrder:
54	    expression: BoundExpr | None
55	    output_index: int | None
56	    descending: bool
57	
58	
59	@dataclass(frozen=True)
60	class BoundQuery:
61	    ranges: tuple[Range, ...]
62	    joins: tuple[BoundJoin, ...]
63	    where: BoundExpr | None
64	    group_by: tuple[BoundExpr, ...]
65	    aggregates: tuple[BoundExpr, ...]
66	    aggregate_query: bool
67	    having: BoundExpr | None
68	    select: tuple[BoundExpr, ...]
69	    columns: list[str]
70	    order_by: tuple[BoundOrder, ...]
71	    distinct: bool
72	    limit: int | None
73	    offset: int
74	
75	
76	def bind(query: ast.Query, catalog: Catalog) -> BoundQuery:
77	    return _Binder(query, catalog).bind()
78	
79	
80	class _Binder:
81	    def __init__(self, query: ast.Query, catalog: Catalog) -> None:
82	        self.query = query
83	        self.catalog = catalog
84	        self.ranges: list[Range] = []
85	        self.aggregates: list[BoundExpr] = []
86	
87	    def error(self, message: str, source: ast.Node | Token) -> None:
88	        if isinstance(source, Token):
89	            line, column = source.line, source.column
90	        else:
91	            prefix = self.query.source[:source.start]
92	            line = prefix.count("\n") + 1
93	            column = source.start - prefix.rfind("\n")
94	        raise SemanticError(message, line, column)
95	
96	    def add_range(self, reference: ast.TableRef) -> Range:
97	        token = reference.alias or reference.name
98	        table = self.catalog.load(reference.name.value,
99	                                  reference.name.line, reference.name.column)
100	        if any(r.name.lower() == token.value.lower() for r in self.ranges):
101	            self.error(f"duplicate table name '{token.value}'", token)
102	        offset = sum(len(r.table.columns) for r in self.ranges)
103	        result = Range(token.value, table, offset)
104	        self.ranges.append(result)
105	        return result
106	
107	    def column(self, source: ast.Column) -> BoundExpr:
108	        matches = []
109	        for range_ in self.ranges:
110	            if (source.qualifier is not None
111	                    and range_.name.lower() != source.qualifier.value.lower()):
112	                continue
113	            for index, name in enumerate(range_.table.columns):
114	                if name.lower() == source.name.value.lower():
115	                    matches.append((range_, index))
116	        reference = self.reference(source)
117	        if len(matches) != 1:
118	            adjective = "unknown" if not matches else "ambiguous"
119	            self.error(f"{adjective} column '{reference}'", source)
120	        range_, index = matches[0]
121	        return BoundExpr("column", range_.table.types[index], source,
122	                         value=range_.offset + index)
123	
124	    @staticmethod
125	    def reference(source: ast.Column) -> str:
126	        return ((source.qualifier.value + ".") if source.qualifier else "") + source.name.value
127	
128	    def mismatch(self, operator: Token, *operands: BoundExpr) -> None:
129	        types = " and ".join(operand.type for operand in operands)
130	        name = operator.value.upper() if operator.kind in ("IDENT", "QUOTED_IDENT") else operator.kind
131	        self.error(f"type mismatch: cannot apply '{name}' to {types}", operator)
132	
133	    def comparable(self, left: BoundExpr, right: BoundExpr, operator: Token) -> None:
134	        if (left.type == "NULL" or right.type == "NULL"
135	                or left.type in _NUMERIC and right.type in _NUMERIC
136	                or left.type == right.type == "TEXT"):
137	            return
138	        self.mismatch(operator, left, right)
139	
140	    def condition(self, source: ast.Expr, aggregate: bool = False) -> BoundExpr:
141	        expression = self.expression(source, aggregate)
142	        if expression.type not in _NUMERIC:
143	            self.error(f"condition must be numeric, got {expression.type}", source)
144	        return expression
145	
146	    def expression(self, source: ast.Expr, aggregate: bool) -> BoundExpr:
147	        if isinstance(source, ast.Parenthesized):
148	            return self.expression(source.expression, aggregate)
149	        if isinstance(source, ast.Literal):
150	            type_ = {"INT": "INTEGER", "REAL": "REAL", "STRING": "TEXT", "NULL": "NULL"}[source.token.kind]
151	            value = None if type_ == "NULL" else source.token.value
152	            return BoundExpr("literal", type_, source, value=value)
153	        if isinstance(source, ast.Column):
154	            return self.column(source)
155	        if isinstance(source, ast.Call):
156	            name = source.name.value.lower()
157	            if name not in _AGGREGATES:
158	                self.error(f"unknown function '{source.name.value}'", source.name)
159	            name = name.upper()
160	            if not aggregate:
161	                self.error("aggregate function not allowed here", source.name)
162	            if source.star is not None and name != "COUNT":
163	                self.error("'*' argument only allowed for COUNT", source.star)
164	            children = (() if source.star is not None
165	                        else (self.expression(source.argument, False),))
166	            if name in ("SUM", "AVG") and children[0].type not in _NUMERIC:
167	                self.mismatch(source.name, children[0])
168	            type_ = ("INTEGER" if name == "COUNT" else "REAL" if name == "AVG"
169	                     else children[0].type)
170	            result = BoundExpr("aggregate", type_, source, children, name,
171	                               source.name, len(self.aggregates))
172	            self.aggregates.append(result)
173	            return result
174	        if isinstance(source, ast.Unary):
175	            child = self.expression(source.operand, aggregate)
176	            if child.type not in _NUMERIC:
177	                self.mismatch(source.operator, child)
178	            type_ = "INTEGER" if source.operator.kind == "NOT" else child.type
179	            return BoundExpr("unary", type_, source, (child,),
180	                             source.operator.kind, source.operator)
181	        if isinstance(source, ast.Binary):
182	            left = self.expression(source.left, aggregate)
183	            right = self.expression(source.right, aggregate)
184	            operator = source.operator.kind
185	            if operator in _COMPARISONS:
186	                self.comparable(left, right, source.operator)
187	                type_ = "INTEGER"
188	            else:
189	                if left.type not in _NUMERIC or right.type not in _NUMERIC:
190	                    self.mismatch(source.operator, left, right)
191	                type_ = ("INTEGER" if operator in ("AND", "OR")
192	                         else "REAL" if "REAL" in (left.type, right.type)
193	                         else "NULL" if left.type == right.type == "NULL"
194	                         else "INTEGER")
195	            return BoundExpr("binary", type_, source, (left, right), operator,
196	                             source.operator)
197	        if isinstance(source, ast.IsNull):
198	            child = self.expression(source.operand, aggregate)
199	            return BoundExpr("is_null", "INTEGER", source, (child,),
200	                             source.not_token is not None, source.operator)
201	        if isinstance(source, ast.Like):
202	            left = self.expression(source.operand, aggregate)
203	            right = self.expression(source.pattern, aggregate)
204	            if left.type not in ("TEXT", "NULL") or right.type not in ("TEXT", "NULL"):
205	                self.mismatch(source.operator, left, right)
206	            if source.escape is not None and len(source.escape.value) != 1:
207	                self.error("ESCAPE must be a single character", source.escape)
208	            value = (source.not_token is not None,
209	                     source.escape.value if source.escape is not None else None)
210	            return BoundExpr("like", "INTEGER", source, (left, right), value,
211	                             source.operator)
212	        if isinstance(source, ast.In):
213	            left = self.expression(source.operand, aggregate)
214	            items = tuple(self.expression(item, aggregate) for item in source.items)
215	            for item in items:
216	                self.comparable(left, item, source.operator)
217	            return BoundExpr("in", "INTEGER", source, (left,) + items,
218	                             source.not_token is not None, source.operator)
219	        raise AssertionError(f"unhandled AST expression: {type(source).__name__}")
220	
221	    def grouped(self, expression: BoundExpr, keys: dict[tuple, int]) -> BoundExpr:
222	        if expression.key in keys:
223	            return BoundExpr("group", expression.type, expression.source,
224	                             value=expression.key, slot=keys[expression.key])
225	        if expression.kind in ("aggregate", "literal"):
226	            return expression
227	        if expression.kind == "column":
228	            self.error(f"column '{self.reference(expression.source)}' must appear "
229	                       "in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate", expression.source)
230	        return replace(expression, children=tuple(self.grouped(child, keys)
231	                                                 for child in expression.children))
232	
233	    def bind(self) -> BoundQuery:
234	        query = self.query
235	        joins = []
236	        if query.from_table is not None:
237	            self.add_range(query.from_table)
238	        for join in query.joins:
239	            range_ = self.add_range(join.table)
240	            joins.append(BoundJoin(join.kind, range_, self.condition(join.condition)))
241	        where = self.condition(query.where) if query.where is not None else None
242	        group_by = tuple(self.expression(key, False) for key in query.group_by)
243	        select = []
244	        columns = []
245	        aliases: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
246	        wildcards = []
247	        for item in query.items:
248	            source = item.expression
249	            if isinstance(source, ast.Wildcard):
250	                wildcards.append(source)
251	                ranges = self.ranges
252	                if source.qualifier is not None:
253	                    ranges = [r for r in ranges if r.name.lower() == source.qualifier.value.lower()]
254	                    if not ranges:
255	                        self.error(f"unknown table '{source.qualifier.value}'", source.qualifier)
256	                for range_ in ranges:
257	                    for index, name in enumerate(range_.table.columns):
258	                        select.append(BoundExpr("column", range_.table.types[index],
259	                                                source, value=range_.offset + index))
260	                        columns.append(name)
261	                continue
262	            expression = self.expression(source, True)
263	            if item.alias is not None:
264	                name = item.alias.value
265	                aliases.setdefault(name.lower(), []).append(len(select))
266	            elif isinstance(source, ast.Column):
267	                index = expression.value
268	                range_ = next(r for r in self.ranges
269	                              if r.offset <= index < r.offset + len(r.table.columns))
270	                name = range_.table.columns[index - range_.offset]
271	            else:
272	                name = query.source[source.start:source.end]
273	            select.append(expression)
274	            columns.append(name)
275	        having = self.condition(query.having, True) if query.having is not None else None
276	        order_by = []
277	        for item in query.order_by:
278	            source = item.expression
279	            output_index = None
280	            expression = None
281	            if isinstance(source, ast.Literal) and source.token.kind == "INT":
282	                ordinal = source.token.value
283	                if not 1 <= ordinal <= len(select):
284	                    self.error(f"ORDER BY position {integer_text(ordinal)} is out of range", source)
285	                output_index = ordinal - 1
286	            elif (isinstance(source, ast.Column) and source.qualifier is None
287	                  and source.name.value.lower() in aliases):
288	                matches = aliases[source.name.value.lower()]
289	                if len(matches) != 1:
290	                    self.error(f"ambiguous column '{source.name.value}'", source)
291	                output_index = matches[0]
292	            else:
293	                expression = self.expression(source, True)
294	                if query.distinct is not None and not any(expression.key == e.key for e in select):
295	                    self.error("ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used", source)
296	            order_by.append(BoundOrder(expression, output_index,
297	                                       item.direction is not None and item.direction.kind == "DESC"))
298	        aggregate_query = bool(group_by or query.having is not None or self.aggregates)
299	        if aggregate_query:
300	            if wildcards:
301	                self.error("'*' not allowed in aggregate query", wildcards[0].star)
302	            keys = {expression.key: index for index, expression in enumerate(group_by)}
303	            select = [self.grouped(expression, keys) for expression in select]
304	            if having is not None:
305	                having = self.grouped(having, keys)
306	            order_by = [replace(order, expression=self.grouped(order.expression, keys))
307	                        if order.expression is not None else order for order in order_by]
308	        return BoundQuery(tuple(self.ranges), tuple(joins), where, group_by,
309	                          tuple(self.aggregates), aggregate_query, having, tuple(select),
310	                          columns, tuple(order_by), query.distinct is not None,
311	                          query.limit.value if query.limit is not None else None,
312	                          query.offset.value if query.offset is not None else 0)

1	# minisql Feature Specification
2	
3	**Status:** Planned — plan review READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION (see review-plan.md)
4	**Dependencies:** Python 3.11+ standard library; pytest for tests only
5	**Layer:** Query engine / library / CLI
6	**Priority:** Critical path: all contract requirements
7	**Estimated Complexity:** 6 bounded tasks across 3 implementation phases (finalized in implementation-plan.md)
8	
9	## 1. Executive Summary
10	
11	Implement a handwritten, read-only SQL engine over CSV files, with a flat `minisql/` package, library API, deterministic CSV/table rendering, one-shot CLI and REPL. `../../contract.md` is authoritative in full, including R1–R21 and AC12. This document organizes that contract; it does not narrow or replace it. `../../brief.md` additionally requires recognizable tokenizer, AST parser, semantic analyzer and executor layers and pytest tests.
12	
13	Research completed with three independent researchers: repository/acceptance analyst `af392ba25adfa556c`, language/semantics researcher `a483bed12b1e836ca`, data/interface researcher `ae056d83d393a869d`. See `research.md` for findings, sources and limitations.
14	
15	## 2. Problem Statement
16	
17	### Current State
18	
19	The seed repository has only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and `.gitignore`; no application, tests or repository-local AGENTS/CLAUDE guidance. No existing integration surface or prior spec convention constrains module names beyond the required package layout. [Research: repository analyst; contract constraints]
20	
21	### Impact of Inaction
22	
23	There is no executable engine or API. A generic SQL approximation would fail the bespoke arithmetic, source naming, aggregate legality, error and exact-output requirements. Every explicit rule, not merely AC1–AC11, is required by AC12.
24	
25	## 3. Goals & Non-Goals
26	
27	### Goals
28	
29	- Implement all R1–R21 and exact AC1–AC12 behavior.
30	- Expose `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]` and `minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`.
31	- Use Python >=3.11, stdlib runtime imports only; no sqlite3, existing SQL engine or parser.
32	- Deterministic ordering, UTF-8/LF output, exact classes/messages/positions, no partial one-shot output or tracebacks for specified failures.
33	- Contract-derived pytest coverage including errors, empty inputs, stage ordering, byte-level CLI/REPL and data edge cases.
34	
35	### Non-goals
36	
37	Writes, DDL, subqueries, SQL beyond the supplied grammar, database compatibility, third-party runtime dependencies, query optimizations that change required evaluation, network services, release/deploy/publication.
38	
39	**Assumption:** portability is implemented through standard-library behavior and tested locally; unavailable OS/runtime executions must be reported, not claimed.
40	
41	## 4. Architecture
42	
43	Proposed separable surfaces (planning may refine file names, never required behavior):
44	
45	1. Errors and immutable-shaped Result API.
46	2. Lexer: complete token stream with source offsets and positions.
47	3. Parser/AST: handwritten recursive descent matching contract grammar and precedence, retaining parentheses and source spans.
48	4. Catalog/loader: directory validation, discovery, strict CSV reading, whole-column inference.
49	5. Semantic binder: scoped names, resolved column identity, static types, aggregate legality, structural grouping/DISTINCT/ORDER validation.
50	6. Executor: explicit ordered materialized stages, typed nullable values, aggregate collection, stable sort.
51	7. Formatters and CLI/REPL: pure formatting separate from transport and stream configuration.
52	
53	`connect` validates the directory immediately. Thereafter execute follows lex → parse → semantic (including referenced-table IO in FROM order) → execute. Binding completes before any row expression is evaluated, including empty/unreachable branches. Do not stream output until execute and formatting succeed. [Contract R7, R16–R21; lines 113, 138–143, 189, 205]
54	
55	## 5. Detailed Design
56	
57	### 5.1 Data and schema (R2–R3)
58	
59	- Discover only direct regular files with case-insensitive `.csv` extension; table name is stem, lookup case-insensitive. Colliding lowercase stems raise `ambiguous table file` only when referenced. `tables()` returns stems sorted by `(lower(), name)` without opening content.
60	- Read referenced files anew per execute using `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''`, `csv.reader(..., strict=True)` default dialect. Never read unrelated files. Preserve raw contents, BOM handling, quoted CR/LF and whitespace.
61	- Skip zero-field records, choose first nonzero-field record as header (decision D1). Header names verbatim; reject empty names and case-insensitive duplicates using second occurrence spelling.
62	- Enforce record width using reader.line_num after the record. Catch csv.Error with its current reader.line_num; invalid UTF-8 has the fixed template.
63	- Inference scans every nonempty field without trimming. Full ASCII integer regex first; else full contract REAL regex; else TEXT verbatim. Empty raw field → None; all-empty column → TEXT. Convert numeric-looking strings only once whole-column type is known.
64	
65	Sources: contract lines 105–116; Python csv reader/line_num and TextIOWrapper documentation in `research.md`.
66	
67	### 5.2 Lexing and parsing (R4–R6)
68	
69	Implement the exact EBNF and precedence in contract lines 36–86. Reserved keywords are exactly the listed set; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers. Names and keywords resolve case-insensitively using `lower()`, while source spelling is retained.
70	
71	Whitespace is space/tab/CR/LF only; `--` ends at LF. Only LF advances line. Tabs, CR and Unicode each count one code point. Quoted identifiers allow doubled double quotes and arbitrary content. Strings allow doubled single quotes, multiline content and literal backslashes.
72	
73	Recognize integer and real forms using ASCII digit patterns. A number immediately followed by ASCII alphanumeric, underscore or dot is invalid at the literal start. Signs are unary. Comparisons/predicates are non-associative; chained comparisons fail at the second operator. Calls accept exactly one expression or star. IN is nonempty. FROM is optional (one empty row). LIMIT/OFFSET accept only unsigned integer literal tokens; OFFSET is independently optional; at most one terminal semicolon.
74	
75	Retain token raw source, decoded value, span, line/column, and AST parentheses. Parentheses affect output names and bare ORDER recognition, but not structural identity (D5).
76	
77	### 5.3 Static typing and operators (R7–R9)
78	
79	Types: INTEGER/int, REAL/float, TEXT/str, NULL for bare NULL-derived null expressions. Values may be None; predicates return 1/0/None, never bool.
80	
81	- Numeric arithmetic accepts INTEGER/REAL/NULL; REAL wins, else both NULL → NULL, else INTEGER. Unary signs retain operand type.
82	- Comparisons and each IN item require numeric pairs, TEXT pairs, or either NULL type. TEXT uses Python code-point order.
83	- LIKE accepts TEXT/NULL. Logical operands and WHERE/ON/HAVING conditions must be numeric/NULL.
84	- NULL arithmetic propagates before zero-divisor checking. Exact integer quotient truncates toward zero without float conversion; remainder is dividend-signed. REAL remainder uses math.fmod.
85	- Full 3VL: NULL comparisons unknown; IS returns integer boolean. AND short-circuits only false LHS; OR only true LHS; NULL LHS still evaluates RHS.
86	- IN truth results follow contract; evaluate all non-NULL-LHS list items left-to-right before membership decision (D3). NULL LHS returns NULL.
87	- LIKE is whole-string, case-sensitive, supports newline/Unicode. `%` any sequence, `_` one character. ESCAPE is one-character STRING checked statically. Invalid escaped pattern sequence or trailing escape is runtime at LIKE; NULL operands return NULL first.
88	
89	Sources: contract lines 88–103. SUM/AVG NULL-type policy is recorded in D2, not borrowed from another SQL dialect.
90	
91	### 5.4 Resolution, projection and joins (R6, R10–R11)
92	
93	Bind columns to stable resolved table/column identities. Unqualified search spans current visible ranges; zero matches unknown, multiple ambiguous. Alias hides original table qualifier. Reject duplicate range names at the second range-name token. Each ON sees only its join prefix.
94	
95	Expand `*`/`q.*` in FROM/header order; output duplicates are legal. Name outputs by explicit alias, else unparenthesized column's exact CSV header, else exact first-to-last item-expression source slice (not alias text). No implicit output-name namespace for WHERE/GROUP/HAVING.
96	
97	Joins associate left with literal nested loops: left rows outer, right file rows inner; evaluate ON on every pair, retain true only. LEFT unmatched rows append one NULL-filled right side. NULL never equals NULL in ON.
98	
99	Sources: contract lines 74, 118–122, 140.
100	
101	### 5.5 Aggregation and grouping (R12)
102	
103	Aggregate query if GROUP BY, HAVING, or any aggregate call in SELECT/ORDER BY (HAVING itself establishes aggregate mode). COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(e) non-NULL; SUM INTEGER/REAL preserves numeric type; AVG REAL; MIN/MAX retain argument type. All ignore NULL, COUNT empty → 0, others → None. Only COUNT accepts star. SUM/AVG accept NULL as numeric-compatible (D2); SUM(NULL) type NULL, AVG(NULL) REAL.
104	
105	No GROUP BY → one global group even after empty WHERE. Explicit grouping over empty input → zero groups. First-seen group order; None equals None for keys. Collect every aggregate across SELECT/HAVING/ORDER. Evaluate group keys and aggregate arguments for surviving input rows before HAVING. Do not lazily defer arguments until projection.
106	
107	Select/HAVING/ORDER expressions must recursively consist of aggregate calls, literals and subexpressions structurally identical to a GROUP key. Match resolved columns, normalized keyword operators, typed literal values and operand order. Parentheses are transparent; alternate numeric spellings of same type/value match. Do not perform algebraic normalization or conflate `!=` and `<>` (D5). No star projections in aggregate queries; no aggregates in WHERE/ON/GROUP or inside an aggregate.
108	
109	Sources: contract lines 124–129, 138–143.
110	
111	### 5.6 Ordering, DISTINCT and slicing (R13–R16)
112	
113	- Bare INTEGER ORDER expression is 1-based ordinal after star expansion. `(1)`, `+1`, REAL literals are expressions, not ordinals.
114	- Bare unqualified identifier matching exactly one explicit select alias refers to that output, taking precedence over input; two aliases → ambiguity. Otherwise bind input/group expression.
115	- DISTINCT ORDER must be ordinal, alias or structurally equal to a select expression.
116	- Evaluate stages exactly: FROM/joins → WHERE → all group keys/aggregate arguments → HAVING → projection → ORDER keys → first-occurrence DISTINCT → stable multi-key sort → OFFSET → LIMIT.
117	- NULL smallest; ascending first, descending last. Stable descending ties too. Numeric comparisons mixed freely; text by Python str ordering.
118	- LIMIT 0 does not suppress earlier evaluation/failures. OFFSET past end returns zero rows.
119	
120	Sources: contract lines 131–143.
121	
122	### 5.7 API and formatting (R17–R18)
123	
124	Export connect, Connection, frozen dataclass Result(columns: list[str], types: list[str], rows: list[tuple]), format_csv, format_table and all required errors. connect accepts str/PathLike; schema returns `(header, type)` tuples in header order. No import-time changes to host streams.
125	
126	INTEGER uses str, REAL repr, TEXT verbatim. CSV custom quoting: NULL empty/unquoted; empty string quoted; quote iff empty string, comma, quote, CR/LF, or starts/ends with literal space; double internal quotes. Headers same. Every record LF.
127	
128	Table: escape actual CR/LF to visible `\\r`/`\\n` before width measurement; same for headers (D4). Width code points; header left, numeric values right, TEXT/NULL left. Join with ` | `; separator `-+-`; strip trailing spaces on every line; `(N rows)`/`(1 row)`; final LF.
129	
130	Sources: contract lines 145–170; Python io docs.
131	
132	### 5.8 CLI and REPL (R19–R20)
133	
134	Configure CLI stdout/stderr UTF-8 with LF (not at library import). argparse usage errors exit 2 (D6). Missing/non-directory data fails before SQL lexing, exit 3. Query failures exit 1; success 0. Complete result before writing; error stdout empty and stderr exact single error line plus LF.
135	
136	No SQL → REPL, default table; one-shot default CSV; explicit --format overrides either. Prompt always stdout flushed even non-TTY: `minisql> ` empty buffer else `   ...> `. Empty-buffer blank input ignored; stripped dot-prefix line is command. Other lines append joined LF. Execute/clear when right-stripped buffer ends `;`, without SQL-aware completion. Commands .help, .tables, .schema NAME, .format csv|table, .quit/.exit. Unknown command fixed stderr text. Errors continue. EOF executes nonempty buffer then returns 0 with no further output; prompt already emitted before EOF remains.
137	
138	Sources: contract lines 168–189.
139	
140	### 5.9 Errors (R21)
141	
142	Implement every template and position in contract lines 191–205 verbatim. Export MiniSQLError(Exception), LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, QueryRuntimeError, DataIOError; kind Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime/IO; message and line/column attributes (both None for IO). SQL string format `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO `IOError: <message>`.
143	
144	Names in errors preserve query spelling without quotes; refs qualified as q.c. Operators keywords and aggregate names uppercase; symbols as written. Duplicate range name at second alias/table name token; call star error at internal star; invalid ESCAPE length at string; division at operator; invalid LIKE at LIKE. EOF at one past last source character, with LF-only position accounting. IO file names basenames. Single-error oracle means no invented tie-break requirements among unrelated competing semantic errors.
145	
146	## 6. Cost Estimates
147	
148	No external service/package costs. Primary cost is implementation and contract-edge testing. No optional web expansion needed. Runtime availability risk: default available Python is 3.9.6; installed 3.14 and 3.14-intel64 exit via SIGKILL (-9) before `--version`. Do not install without authorization; test on available runtime with a clearly recorded supported-runtime gap if no working >=3.11 is found. Product must remain Python 3.11+ compatible regardless.
149	
150	## 7. Task Outline (Preliminary)
151	
152	1. Foundation: errors, result, tokens, AST/parser and catalog/inference (independent surfaces).
153	2. Typed binding and execution: static resolution/typing, grouping/order legality, full stage pipeline and operators.
154	3. Interfaces and integration: API, formatters, CLI/REPL, comprehensive regression and acceptance traceability.
155

157	
158	## 8. Risks & Mitigations
159	
160	| Risk | Mitigation |
161	|---|---|
162	| Generic SQL assumptions diverge | Contract-derived tests; no SQL engine oracle |
163	| Lost source/bare metadata | Retain token and AST spans/parentheses; separate structural keys |
164	| Lazy/fused execution changes error order | Explicit materialized stage barriers and fault-order tests |
165	| Incorrect nullable static types | Bind before execute; test empty/unreachable branches |
166	| Group matching too permissive | Resolved structural keys; no algebraic rewrites |
167	| CSV newline/physical-line changes | Required open/reader configuration; byte fixtures |
168	| Cross-platform output drift | Custom quote function, stream reconfigure, golden bytes |
169	| Host runtime limits | Record exact failed launch evidence and local runtime; do not claim unrun platforms |
170	
171	### Recorded decisions and alternatives
172	
173	All decisions are also in mutable `handoff.md`. They resolve underspecified edges only; explicit contract always wins.
174	
175	- **D1:** Skip all zero-field CSV records, including before header; first nonempty record is header. Alternative: literal first record header. Reason: general skip rule is closest evidence.
176	- **D2:** NULL is permitted for SUM/AVG as numeric-compatible; SUM(NULL) has NULL static type, AVG(NULL) REAL; both value None. Alternative: reject bare NULL as nonnumeric. Reason: consistent NULL operand acceptance and all-null aggregate outcomes; no defined SUM(NULL) type otherwise.
177	- **D3:** IN with NULL LHS returns NULL; otherwise evaluate all items left-to-right before deciding membership. Alternative: stop at first match. Reason: only AND/OR explicitly authorize short circuit; avoid hiding failures.
178	- **D4:** Escape CR/LF in table headers as in cell text. Alternative: retain literal newlines. Reason: headers are cells and aligned table remains deterministic.
179	- **D5:** Structural keys ignore parentheses/source spelling, compare typed literal value, preserve symbol spelling and operand order; lowercase resolved names. Alternative: source-text keys / normalize comparison synonyms. Reason: same resolved columns/operators/literals, no algebraic extension.
180	- **D6:** Standard argparse usage diagnostics apply to exit 2; exact single-line engine-error requirement applies to specified query/data errors. Malformed dot-command arguments use unknown-command text. schema unknown table uses SemanticError at 1:1. Unlisted OS read failures become DataIOError with stable basename and OS description where possible. Alternative: invent new templates. Reason: preserve defined behavior; no new public query error template.
181	- **D7:** No runtime installation; use available tests and report unsupported-runtime/platform execution honestly. Alternative: external installation. Reason: no external-install authority and no need to change product constraints.
182	
183	No researchers disagreed on an explicit requirement. Unresolved policies and alternatives above are orchestrator decisions, not changes to contract authority.

58	## Engine design details
59	
60	### Lex / parse
61	
62	Handwritten complete lexer, recursive-descent parser. Positions code points, LF-only lines. Exact ASCII regexes, malformed continuation checks; signs separate. Precedence and non-associative comparison exact. Quoted names/strings decode doubles while retaining original spans. Full tokenize before parse. Parenthesis node/flag preserved for headings/bare ORDER but ignored for structural keys. No FROM yields one empty row.
63	
64	### Semantic
65	
66	Load referenced CSVs in FROM order after parse; no unrelated reads. Scoped ON binding per introduced prefix; aliases hide original qualifiers, duplicate ranges positioned at second range token. Expand wildcards; preserve output headers. Bind resolved column indexes and static types for every expression irrespective of rows, filters, short circuit or pagination. Type operators and conditions exactly, no bool outputs.
67

63	        if self.match("GROUP"):
64	            self.expect("BY")
65	            group_by.append(self.expression())
66	            while self.match(","):
67	                group_by.append(self.expression())
68	        having = self.expression() if self.match("HAVING") else None
69	        order_by = []
70	        if self.match("ORDER"):
71	            self.expect("BY")
72	            order_by.append(self.order())
73	            while self.match(","):
74	                order_by.append(self.order())
75	        limit = self.expect("INT") if self.match("LIMIT") else None
76	        offset = self.expect("INT") if self.match("OFFSET") else None
77	        semicolon = self.match(";")
78	        end = self.tokens[self.index - 1].end
79	        self.expect("EOF")
80	        return ast.Query(
81	            select.start, end, self.source, select, distinct, tuple(items),
82	            from_table, tuple(joins), where, tuple(group_by), having,
83	            tuple(order_by), limit, offset, semicolon,
84	        )
85	
86	    def alias(self) -> tuple[Token | None, Token | None]:
87	        as_token = self.match("AS")
88	        alias = self.expect(*_NAMES) if as_token else self.match(*_NAMES)
89	        return alias, as_token
90	
91	    def item(self) -> ast.SelectItem:
92	        token = self.current
93	        if star := self.match("*"):
94	            expression = ast.Wildcard(star.start, star.end, star, None)
95	        elif (token.kind in _NAMES
96	              and self.tokens[self.index + 1].kind == "."
97	              and self.tokens[self.index + 2].kind == "*"):
98	            qualifier = self.expect(*_NAMES)
99	            self.expect(".")
100	            star = self.expect("*")
101	            expression = ast.Wildcard(qualifier.start, star.end, star, qualifier)
102	        else:
103	            expression = self.expression()
104	            alias, as_token = self.alias()
105	            end = alias.end if alias else expression.end
106	            return ast.SelectItem(expression.start, end, expression, alias,
107	                                  as_token)
108	        return ast.SelectItem(expression.start, expression.end, expression,
109	                              None, None)
110	
111	    def table(self) -> ast.TableRef:
112	        name = self.expect(*_NAMES)
113	        alias, as_token = self.alias()
114	        return ast.TableRef(name.start, alias.end if alias else name.end,
115	                            name, alias, as_token)
116	
117	    def join(self) -> ast.Join:
118	        keyword = self.expect("JOIN", "INNER", "LEFT")
119	        kind = "LEFT" if keyword.kind == "LEFT" else "INNER"
120	        outer = self.match("OUTER") if kind == "LEFT" else None
121	        join_token = keyword if keyword.kind == "JOIN" else self.expect("JOIN")
122	        table = self.table()
123	        on_token = self.expect("ON")
124	        condition = self.expression()
125	        return ast.Join(keyword.start, condition.end, kind, table, condition,
126	                        keyword, join_token, outer, on_token)
127	
128	    def order(self) -> ast.OrderItem:
129	        expression = self.expression()
130	        direction = self.match("ASC", "DESC")
131	        return ast.OrderItem(expression.start,
132	                             direction.end if direction else expression.end,
133	                             expression, direction)
134	
135	    def binary(self, operand, operators: tuple[str, ...]) -> ast.Expr:
136	        left = operand()
137	        while self.current.kind in operators:
138	            operator = self.expect(*operators)
139	            right = operand()
140	            left = ast.Binary(left.start, right.end, left, operator, right)
141	        return left
142	
143	    def expression(self) -> ast.Expr:
144	        return self.binary(self.and_expression, ("OR",))
145	
146	    def and_expression(self) -> ast.Expr:
147	        return self.binary(self.not_expression, ("AND",))
148	
149	    def not_expression(self) -> ast.Expr:
150	        if operator := self.match("NOT"):
151	            operand = self.not_expression()
152	            return ast.Unary(operator.start, operand.end, operator, operand)
153	        return self.comparison()
154	
155	    def comparison(self) -> ast.Expr:
156	        left = self.add()
157	        if operator := self.match(*_COMPARISONS):
158	            right = self.add()
159	            return ast.Binary(left.start, right.end, left, operator, right)
160	        if operator := self.match("IS"):
161	            not_token = self.match("NOT")
162	            null = self.expect("NULL")
163	            return ast.IsNull(left.start, null.end, left, operator, not_token,
164	                              null)
165	        not_token = self.match("NOT")
166	        if operator := self.match("LIKE"):
167	            pattern = self.add()
168	            escape_keyword = self.match("ESCAPE")
169	            escape = self.expect("STRING") if escape_keyword else None
170	            return ast.Like(left.start, escape.end if escape else pattern.end,
171	                            left, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword,
172	                            escape)
173	        if operator := self.match("IN"):
174	            lparen = self.expect("(")
175	            items = [self.expression()]
176	            while self.match(","):
177	                items.append(self.expression())
178	            rparen = self.expect(")")
179	            return ast.In(left.start, rparen.end, left, operator, tuple(items),
180	                          not_token, lparen, rparen)
181	        if not_token:
182	            self.error()
183	        return left
184	
185	    def add(self) -> ast.Expr:
186	        return self.binary(self.multiply, ("+", "-"))
187	
188	    def multiply(self) -> ast.Expr:
189	        return self.binary(self.unary, ("*", "/", "%"))
190	
191	    def unary(self) -> ast.Expr:
192	        if operator := self.match("+", "-"):
193	            operand = self.unary()
194	            return ast.Unary(operator.start, operand.end, operator, operand)
195	        return self.primary()
196	
197	    def primary(self) -> ast.Expr:
198	        if token := self.match("INT", "REAL", "STRING", "NULL"):
199	            return ast.Literal(token.start, token.end, token)
200	        if lparen := self.match("("):
201	            expression = self.expression()
202	            rparen = self.expect(")")
203	            return ast.Parenthesized(lparen.start, rparen.end, expression,
204	                                     lparen, rparen)
205	        name = self.expect(*_NAMES)
206	        if lparen := self.match("("):
207	            star = self.match("*")
208	            argument = None if star else self.expression()
209	            rparen = self.expect(")")
210	            return ast.Call(name.start, rparen.end, name, argument, star,
211	                            lparen, rparen)
212	        if self.match("."):
213	            column = self.expect(*_NAMES)
214	            return ast.Column(name.start, column.end, column, name)
215	        return ast.Column(name.start, name.end, name, None)

1	"""Handwritten SQL lexer with code-point offsets and LF-only positions."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	import re
7	
8	from .errors import LexError
9	from .model import parse_integer
10	
11	
12	KEYWORDS = frozenset(
13	    "SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET "
14	    "AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN".split()
15	)
16	_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
17	_NUMBER = re.compile(
18	    r"(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
19	    r"|[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+|[0-9]+"
20	)
21	
22	
23	@dataclass(frozen=True)
24	class Token:
25	    kind: str
26	    raw: str
27	    value: str | int | float | None
28	    start: int
29	    end: int
30	    line: int
31	    column: int
32	
33	
34	def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
35	    """Tokenize the entire source, including a positioned terminal EOF token.
36	
37	    Kinds are INT, REAL, STRING, IDENT, QUOTED_IDENT, EOF, uppercase reserved
38	    keywords, or the operator/punctuation itself. Offsets are zero-based and
39	    end-exclusive; line/column are one-based. Values decode quotes/numbers;
40	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
41	    """
42	    tokens = []
43	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1
44	
45	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
46	        nonlocal i, line, column
47	        text = sql[i:end]
48	        newlines = text.count("\n")
49	        if newlines:
50	            line += newlines
51	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1
52	        else:
53	            column += end - i
54	        i = end
55	
56	    while i < len(sql):
57	        char = sql[i]
58	        if char in " \t\r\n":
59	            advance(i + 1)
60	            continue
61	        if sql.startswith("--", i):
62	            end = sql.find("\n", i)
63	            advance(len(sql) if end == -1 else end)
64	            continue
65	
66	        start, token_line, token_column = i, line, column
67	        if char in "\"'":
68	            quote = char
69	            end = i + 1
70	            decoded = []
71	            while end < len(sql):
72	                if sql[end] == quote:
73	                    if end + 1 < len(sql) and sql[end + 1] == quote:
74	                        decoded.append(quote)
75	                        end += 2
76	                        continue
77	                    end += 1
78	                    break
79	                decoded.append(sql[end])
80	                end += 1
81	            else:
82	                description = ("string literal" if quote == "'"
83	                               else "quoted identifier")
84	                raise LexError(f"unterminated {description}", line, column)
85	            kind = "STRING" if quote == "'" else "QUOTED_IDENT"
86	            value = "".join(decoded)
87	        elif "0" <= char <= "9" or (
88	            char == "." and i + 1 < len(sql) and "0" <= sql[i + 1] <= "9"
89	        ):
90	            match = _NUMBER.match(sql, i)
91	            end = match.end()
92	            if end < len(sql) and (
93	                sql[end].isalpha() or sql[end].isdigit() or sql[end] in "_."
94	            ):
95	                raise LexError("invalid number literal", line, column)
96	            raw = match.group()
97	            kind = "REAL" if any(c in raw for c in ".eE") else "INT"
98	            value = float(raw) if kind == "REAL" else parse_integer(raw)
99	        elif match := _NAME.match(sql, i):
100	            end = match.end()
101	            raw = match.group()
102	            kind = raw.upper() if raw.upper() in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
103	            value = raw if kind == "IDENT" else kind
104	        elif sql[i:i + 2] in ("<>", "!=", "<=", ">="):
105	            end = i + 2
106	            kind = value = sql[i:end]
107	        elif char in "+-*/%=<>(),.;":
108	            end = i + 1
109	            kind = value = char
110	        else:
111	            raise LexError(f"unexpected character '{char}'", line, column)
112	        tokens.append(Token(kind, sql[start:end], value, start, end,
113	                            token_line, token_column))
114	        advance(end)
115	
116	    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", None, i, i, line, column))
117	    return tokens
118

15	def parse_integer(text: str) -> int:
16	    """Convert validated, optionally signed ASCII decimal digits in chunks."""
17	    negative = text.startswith("-")
18	    if text[:1] in ("+", "-"):
19	        text = text[1:]
20	    value = int(text[:9])
21	    for start in range(9, len(text), 9):
22	        chunk = text[start:start + 9]
23	        value = value * 10 ** len(chunk) + int(chunk)
24	    return -value if negative else value
25	
26	
27	def integer_text(value: int) -> str:
28	    """Render an arbitrary-size integer without unbounded decimal conversion."""
29	    sign = "-" if value < 0 else ""
30	    value = abs(value)
31	    chunks = []
32	    while value >= 1_000_000_000:
33	        value, chunk = divmod(value, 1_000_000_000)
34	        chunks.append(str(chunk).zfill(9))
35	    chunks.append(str(value))
36	    return sign + "".join(reversed(chunks))

1	"""Recursive-descent parser for exactly the contract's SELECT grammar."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from . import ast
6	from .errors import ParseError
7	from .lexer import Token, tokenize
8	
9	
10	_NAMES = ("IDENT", "QUOTED_IDENT")
11	_COMPARISONS = ("=", "<>", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
12	
13	
14	def parse(sql: str) -> ast.Query:
15	    """Lex the complete input before parsing, then return its sourceful AST."""
16	    return _Parser(sql, tokenize(sql)).query()
17	
18	
19	class _Parser:
20	    def __init__(self, source: str, tokens: list[Token]) -> None:
21	        self.source = source
22	        self.tokens = tokens
23	        self.index = 0
24	
25	    @property
26	    def current(self) -> Token:
27	        return self.tokens[self.index]
28	
29	    def error(self) -> None:
30	        token = self.current
31	        message = ("unexpected end of input" if token.kind == "EOF"
32	                   else f"unexpected token '{token.raw}'")
33	        raise ParseError(message, token.line, token.column)
34	
35	    def match(self, *kinds: str) -> Token | None:
36	        if self.current.kind in kinds:
37	            token = self.current
38	            self.index += 1
39	            return token
40	        return None
41	
42	    def expect(self, *kinds: str) -> Token:
43	        token = self.match(*kinds)
44	        if token is None:
45	            self.error()
46	        return token
47	
48	    def query(self) -> ast.Query:
49	        select = self.expect("SELECT")
50	        distinct = self.match("DISTINCT")
51	        items = [self.item()]
52	        while self.match(","):
53	            items.append(self.item())
54	
55	        from_table = None
56	        joins = []
57	        if self.match("FROM"):
58	            from_table = self.table()
59	            while self.current.kind in ("JOIN", "INNER", "LEFT"):
60	                joins.append(self.join())
61	        where = self.expression() if self.match("WHERE") else None
62	        group_by = []
63	        if self.match("GROUP"):
64	            self.expect("BY")
65	            group_by.append(self.expression())
66	            while self.match(","):
67	                group_by.append(self.expression())
68	        having = self.expression() if self.match("HAVING") else None
69	        order_by = []
70	        if self.match("ORDER"):
71	            self.expect("BY")
72	            order_by.append(self.order())
73	            while self.match(","):
74	                order_by.append(self.order())
75	        limit = self.expect("INT") if self.match("LIMIT") else None
76	        offset = self.expect("INT") if self.match("OFFSET") else None
77	        semicolon = self.match(";")
78	        end = self.tokens[self.index - 1].end
79	        self.expect("EOF")
80	        return ast.Query(
81	            select.start, end, self.source, select, distinct, tuple(items),
82	            from_table, tuple(joins), where, tuple(group_by), having,
83	            tuple(order_by), limit, offset, semicolon,
84	        )
85	
86	    def alias(self) -> tuple[Token | None, Token | None]:
87	        as_token = self.match("AS")
88	        alias = self.expect(*_NAMES) if as_token else self.match(*_NAMES)
89	        return alias, as_token
90	
91	    def item(self) -> ast.SelectItem:
92	        token = self.current
93	        if star := self.match("*"):
94	            expression = ast.Wildcard(star.start, star.end, star, None)
95	        elif (token.kind in _NAMES
96	              and self.tokens[self.index + 1].kind == "."
97	              and self.tokens[self.index + 2].kind == "*"):
98	            qualifier = self.expect(*_NAMES)
99	            self.expect(".")
100	            star = self.expect("*")
101	            expression = ast.Wildcard(qualifier.start, star.end, star, qualifier)
102	        else:
103	            expression = self.expression()
104	            alias, as_token = self.alias()
105	            end = alias.end if alias else expression.end
106	            return ast.SelectItem(expression.start, end, expression, alias,
107	                                  as_token)
108	        return ast.SelectItem(expression.start, expression.end, expression,
109	                              None, None)
110	
111	    def table(self) -> ast.TableRef:
112	        name = self.expect(*_NAMES)
113	        alias, as_token = self.alias()
114	        return ast.TableRef(name.start, alias.end if alias else name.end,
115	                            name, alias, as_token)
116	
117	    def join(self) -> ast.Join:
118	        keyword = self.expect("JOIN", "INNER", "LEFT")
119	        kind = "LEFT" if keyword.kind == "LEFT" else "INNER"
120	        outer = self.match("OUTER") if kind == "LEFT" else None
121	        join_token = keyword if keyword.kind == "JOIN" else self.expect("JOIN")
122	        table = self.table()
123	        on_token = self.expect("ON")
124	        condition = self.expression()
125	        return ast.Join(keyword.start, condition.end, kind, table, condition,
126	                        keyword, join_token, outer, on_token)
127	
128	    def order(self) -> ast.OrderItem:
129	        expression = self.expression()
130	        direction = self.match("ASC", "DESC")
131	        return ast.OrderItem(expression.start,
132	                             direction.end if direction else expression.end,
133	                             expression, direction)
134	
135	    def binary(self, operand, operators: tuple[str, ...]) -> ast.Expr:
136	        left = operand()
137	        while self.current.kind in operators:
138	            operator = self.expect(*operators)
139	            right = operand()
140	            left = ast.Binary(left.start, right.end, left, operator, right)
141	        return left
142	
143	    def expression(self) -> ast.Expr:
144	        return self.binary(self.and_expression, ("OR",))
145	
146	    def and_expression(self) -> ast.Expr:
147	        return self.binary(self.not_expression, ("AND",))
148	
149	    def not_expression(self) -> ast.Expr:
150	        if operator := self.match("NOT"):
151	            operand = self.not_expression()
152	            return ast.Unary(operator.start, operand.end, operator, operand)
153	        return self.comparison()
154	
155	    def comparison(self) -> ast.Expr:
156	        left = self.add()
157	        if operator := self.match(*_COMPARISONS):
158	            right = self.add()
159	            return ast.Binary(left.start, right.end, left, operator, right)
160	        if operator := self.match("IS"):
161	            not_token = self.match("NOT")
162	            null = self.expect("NULL")
163	            return ast.IsNull(left.start, null.end, left, operator, not_token,
164	                              null)
165	        not_token = self.match("NOT")
166	        if operator := self.match("LIKE"):
167	            pattern = self.add()
168	            escape_keyword = self.match("ESCAPE")
169	            escape = self.expect("STRING") if escape_keyword else None
170	            return ast.Like(left.start, escape.end if escape else pattern.end,
171	                            left, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword,
172	                            escape)
173	        if operator := self.match("IN"):
174	            lparen = self.expect("(")
175	            items = [self.expression()]
176	            while self.match(","):
177	                items.append(self.expression())
178	            rparen = self.expect(")")
179	            return ast.In(left.start, rparen.end, left, operator, tuple(items),
180	                          not_token, lparen, rparen)
181	        if not_token:
182	            self.error()
183	        return left
184	
185	    def add(self) -> ast.Expr:
186	        return self.binary(self.multiply, ("+", "-"))
187	
188	    def multiply(self) -> ast.Expr:
189	        return self.binary(self.unary, ("*", "/", "%"))
190	
191	    def unary(self) -> ast.Expr:
192	        if operator := self.match("+", "-"):
193	            operand = self.unary()
194	            return ast.Unary(operator.start, operand.end, operator, operand)
195	        return self.primary()
196	
197	    def primary(self) -> ast.Expr:
198	        if token := self.match("INT", "REAL", "STRING", "NULL"):
199	            return ast.Literal(token.start, token.end, token)
200	        if lparen := self.match("("):
201	            expression = self.expression()
202	            rparen = self.expect(")")
203	            return ast.Parenthesized(lparen.start, rparen.end, expression,
204	                                     lparen, rparen)
205	        name = self.expect(*_NAMES)
206	        if lparen := self.match("("):
207	            star = self.match("*")
208	            argument = None if star else self.expression()
209	            rparen = self.expect(")")
210	            return ast.Call(name.start, rparen.end, name, argument, star,
211	                            lparen, rparen)
212	        if self.match("."):
213	            column = self.expect(*_NAMES)
214	            return ast.Column(name.start, column.end, column, name)
215	        return ast.Column(name.start, name.end, name, None)

2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	import re
7	
8	from .errors import LexError
9	from .model import parse_integer
10	
11	
12	KEYWORDS = frozenset(
13	    "SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET "
14	    "AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN".split()
15	)
16	_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
17	_NUMBER = re.compile(
18	    r"(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
19	    r"|[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+|[0-9]+"
20	)
21	
22	
23	@dataclass(frozen=True)
24	class Token:
25	    kind: str
26	    raw: str
27	    value: str | int | float | None
28	    start: int
29	    end: int
30	    line: int
31	    column: int
32	
33	
34	def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
35	    """Tokenize the entire source, including a positioned terminal EOF token.
36	
37	    Kinds are INT, REAL, STRING, IDENT, QUOTED_IDENT, EOF, uppercase reserved
38	    keywords, or the operator/punctuation itself. Offsets are zero-based and
39	    end-exclusive; line/column are one-based. Values decode quotes/numbers;
40	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
41	    """
42	    tokens = []
43	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1
44	
45	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
46	        nonlocal i, line, column
47	        text = sql[i:end]
48	        newlines = text.count("\n")
49	        if newlines:
50	            line += newlines
51	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1
52	        else:
53	            column += end - i
54	        i = end
55	
56	    while i < len(sql):
57	        char = sql[i]
58	        if char in " \t\r\n":
59	            advance(i + 1)
60	            continue
61	        if sql.startswith("--", i):
62	            end = sql.find("\n", i)
63	            advance(len(sql) if end == -1 else end)
64	            continue
65	
66	        start, token_line, token_column = i, line, column
67	        if char in "\"'":
68	            quote = char
69	            end = i + 1
70	            decoded = []
71	            while end < len(sql):
72	                if sql[end] == quote:
73	                    if end + 1 < len(sql) and sql[end + 1] == quote:
74	                        decoded.append(quote)
75	                        end += 2
76	                        continue
77	                    end += 1
78	                    break
79	                decoded.append(sql[end])
80	                end += 1
81	            else:
82	                description = ("string literal" if quote == "'"
83	                               else "quoted identifier")
84	                raise LexError(f"unterminated {description}", line, column)
85	            kind = "STRING" if quote == "'" else "QUOTED_IDENT"
86	            value = "".join(decoded)
87	        elif "0" <= char <= "9" or (
88	            char == "." and i + 1 < len(sql) and "0" <= sql[i + 1] <= "9"
89	        ):
90	            match = _NUMBER.match(sql, i)
91	            end = match.end()
92	            if end < len(sql) and (
93	                sql[end].isalpha() or sql[end].isdigit() or sql[end] in "_."
94	            ):
95	                raise LexError("invalid number literal", line, column)
96	            raw = match.group()
97	            kind = "REAL" if any(c in raw for c in ".eE") else "INT"
98	            value = float(raw) if kind == "REAL" else parse_integer(raw)
99	        elif match := _NAME.match(sql, i):
100	            end = match.end()
101	            raw = match.group()
102	            kind = raw.upper() if raw.upper() in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
103	            value = raw if kind == "IDENT" else kind
104	        elif sql[i:i + 2] in ("<>", "!=", "<=", ">="):
105	            end = i + 2
106	            kind = value = sql[i:end]
107	        elif char in "+-*/%=<>(),.;":
108	            end = i + 1
109	            kind = value = char
110	        else:
111	            raise LexError(f"unexpected character '{char}'", line, column)
112	        tokens.append(Token(kind, sql[start:end], value, start, end,
113	                            token_line, token_column))
114	        advance(end)
115	
116	    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", None, i, i, line, column))
117	    return tokens

15	def parse_integer(text: str) -> int:
16	    """Convert validated, optionally signed ASCII decimal digits in chunks."""
17	    negative = text.startswith("-")
18	    if text[:1] in ("+", "-"):
19	        text = text[1:]
20	    value = int(text[:9])
21	    for start in range(9, len(text), 9):
22	        chunk = text[start:start + 9]
23	        value = value * 10 ** len(chunk) + int(chunk)
24	    return -value if negative else value
25	
26	
27	def integer_text(value: int) -> str:
28	    """Render an arbitrary-size integer without unbounded decimal conversion."""
29	    sign = "-" if value < 0 else ""
30	    value = abs(value)
31	    chunks = []
32	    while value >= 1_000_000_000:
33	        value, chunk = divmod(value, 1_000_000_000)
34	        chunks.append(str(chunk).zfill(9))
35	    chunks.append(str(value))
36	    return sign + "".join(reversed(chunks))

78	def test_integer_helpers_signed_zero_padded_and_bounded(monkeypatch, digits):
79	    # Guard module-local builtins, not process-wide conversion settings. The
80	    # nine-digit bound is stricter than Python 3.11's default 4300-digit limit.
81	    def bounded_int(text):
82	        if len(text) > 9:
83	            raise ValueError("unbounded decimal parsing")
84	        return int(text)
85	
86	    def bounded_str(value):
87	        if not 0 <= value < 1_000_000_000:
88	            raise ValueError("unbounded decimal rendering")
89	        return str(value)
90	
91	    get_limit = getattr(sys, "get_int_max_str_digits", lambda: None)
92	    limit = get_limit()
93	    monkeypatch.setattr(model, "int", bounded_int, raising=False)
94	    monkeypatch.setattr(model, "str", bounded_str, raising=False)
95	    raw = "9" * digits
96	    expected = 10 ** digits - 1
97	    for sign in ("", "+", "-"):
98	        value = -expected if sign == "-" else expected
99	        assert model.parse_integer(sign + "000" + raw) == value
100	        assert model.integer_text(value) == ("-" if sign == "-" else "") + raw
101	        assert model.parse_integer(sign + "0" * digits) == 0
102	    assert model.parse_integer("1" + "0" * digits) == 10 ** digits
103	    assert model.integer_text(-(10 ** digits)) == "-1" + "0" * digits
104	    assert model.integer_text(0) == "0"
105	    assert get_limit() == limit

15	def shape(node):
16	    if isinstance(node, ast.Literal):
17	        return node.token.value
18	    if isinstance(node, ast.Column):
19	        return ("column", node.qualifier.value if node.qualifier else None,
20	                node.name.value)
21	    if isinstance(node, ast.Unary):
22	        return (node.operator.kind, shape(node.operand))
23	    if isinstance(node, ast.Binary):
24	        return (node.operator.kind, shape(node.left), shape(node.right))
25	    if isinstance(node, ast.Parenthesized):
26	        return ("parens", shape(node.expression))
27	    raise AssertionError(type(node))

78	def test_integer_helpers_signed_zero_padded_and_bounded(monkeypatch, digits):
79	    # Guard module-local builtins, not process-wide conversion settings. The
80	    # nine-digit bound is stricter than Python 3.11's default 4300-digit limit.
81	    def bounded_int(text):
82	        if len(text) > 9:
83	            raise ValueError("unbounded decimal parsing")
84	        return int(text)
85	
86	    def bounded_str(value):
87	        if not 0 <= value < 1_000_000_000:
88	            raise ValueError("unbounded decimal rendering")
89	        return str(value)
90	
91	    get_limit = getattr(sys, "get_int_max_str_digits", lambda: None)
92	    limit = get_limit()
93	    monkeypatch.setattr(model, "int", bounded_int, raising=False)
94	    monkeypatch.setattr(model, "str", bounded_str, raising=False)
95	    raw = "9" * digits
96	    expected = 10 ** digits - 1
97	    for sign in ("", "+", "-"):
98	        value = -expected if sign == "-" else expected
99	        assert model.parse_integer(sign + "000" + raw) == value
100	        assert model.integer_text(value) == ("-" if sign == "-" else "") + raw
101	        assert model.parse_integer(sign + "0" * digits) == 0
102	    assert model.parse_integer("1" + "0" * digits) == 10 ** digits
103	    assert model.integer_text(-(10 ** digits)) == "-1" + "0" * digits
104	    assert model.integer_text(0) == "0"
105	    assert get_limit() == limit

1	"""Execute bound queries through ordered, materialized contract stages."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	from functools import cmp_to_key
7	import math
8	import re
9	
10	from .errors import QueryRuntimeError
11	from .model import Result
12	from .semantic import BoundExpr, BoundQuery
13	
14	
15	@dataclass(frozen=True)
16	class _Context:
17	    row: tuple = ()
18	    keys: tuple = ()
19	    aggregates: tuple = ()
20	
21	
22	def _truth(value):
23	    return None if value is None else int(value != 0)
24	
25	
26	def _runtime(message: str, expression: BoundExpr) -> None:
27	    token = expression.token
28	    raise QueryRuntimeError(message, token.line, token.column)
29	
30	
31	def _quotient(left: int, right: int) -> int:
32	    value = abs(left) // abs(right)
33	    return -value if (left < 0) != (right < 0) else value
34	
35	
36	def _like(value: str, pattern: str, escape: str | None, expression: BoundExpr) -> int:
37	    pieces = []
38	    index = 0
39	    while index < len(pattern):
40	        character = pattern[index]
41	        if character == escape:
42	            index += 1
43	            if index == len(pattern) or pattern[index] not in ("%", "_", escape):
44	                _runtime("invalid LIKE pattern", expression)
45	            pieces.append(re.escape(pattern[index]))
46	        elif character == "%":
47	            pieces.append(".*")
48	        elif character == "_":
49	            pieces.append(".")
50	        else:
51	            pieces.append(re.escape(character))
52	        index += 1
53	    return int(re.fullmatch("".join(pieces), value, flags=re.DOTALL) is not None)
54	
55	
56	def evaluate(expression: BoundExpr, context: _Context):
57	    """Evaluate a statically checked expression; SQL predicates never return bool."""
58	    kind = expression.kind
59	    if kind == "literal":
60	        return expression.value
61	    if kind == "column":
62	        return context.row[expression.value]
63	    if kind == "group":
64	        return context.keys[expression.slot]
65	    if kind == "aggregate":
66	        return context.aggregates[expression.slot]
67	    if kind == "unary":
68	        value = evaluate(expression.children[0], context)
69	        if value is None:
70	            return None
71	        if expression.value == "NOT":
72	            return 1 - _truth(value)
73	        return -value if expression.value == "-" else +value
74	    if kind == "binary":
75	        operator = expression.value
76	        left = evaluate(expression.children[0], context)
77	        if operator == "AND":
78	            left = _truth(left)
79	            if left == 0:
80	                return 0
81	            right = _truth(evaluate(expression.children[1], context))
82	            return 0 if right == 0 else None if left is None or right is None else 1
83	        if operator == "OR":
84	            left = _truth(left)
85	            if left == 1:
86	                return 1
87	            right = _truth(evaluate(expression.children[1], context))
88	            return 1 if right == 1 else None if left is None or right is None else 0
89	        right = evaluate(expression.children[1], context)
90	        if left is None or right is None:
91	            return None
92	        if operator in ("/", "%"):
93	            if right == 0:
94	                _runtime("division by zero", expression)
95	            if expression.type == "REAL":
96	                return left / right if operator == "/" else math.fmod(left, right)
97	            quotient = _quotient(left, right)
98	            return quotient if operator == "/" else left - quotient * right
99	        if operator == "+":
100	            return left + right
101	        if operator == "-":
102	            return left - right
103	        if operator == "*":
104	            return left * right
105	        if operator == "=":
106	            return int(left == right)
107	        if operator in ("!=", "<>"):
108	            return int(left != right)
109	        if operator == "<":
110	            return int(left < right)
111	        if operator == "<=":
112	            return int(left <= right)
113	        if operator == ">":
114	            return int(left > right)
115	        if operator == ">=":
116	            return int(left >= right)
117	    if kind == "is_null":
118	        value = evaluate(expression.children[0], context)
119	        return int(value is not None) if expression.value else int(value is None)
120	    if kind == "like":
121	        value = evaluate(expression.children[0], context)
122	        pattern = evaluate(expression.children[1], context)
123	        if value is None or pattern is None:
124	            return None
125	        negate, escape = expression.value
126	        result = _like(value, pattern, escape, expression)
127	        return 1 - result if negate else result
128	    if kind == "in":
129	        value = evaluate(expression.children[0], context)
130	        if value is None:
131	            return None
132	        # Only AND/OR may skip a non-NULL-LHS operand. A prior match cannot
133	        # conceal a later list-item failure (decision D3).
134	        items = [evaluate(item, context) for item in expression.children[1:]]
135	        result = (1 if any(item is not None and item == value for item in items)
136	                  else None if any(item is None for item in items) else 0)
137	        return 1 - result if expression.value and result is not None else result
138	    raise AssertionError(f"unhandled bound expression: {kind}")
139	
140	
141	def _joined_rows(query: BoundQuery) -> list[tuple]:
142	    rows = list(query.ranges[0].table.rows) if query.ranges else [()]
143	    for join in query.joins:
144	        joined = []
145	        for left in rows:
146	            matched = False
147	            for right in join.range.table.rows:
148	                row = left + right
149	                if _truth(evaluate(join.condition, _Context(row))) == 1:
150	                    joined.append(row)
151	                    matched = True
152	            if join.kind == "LEFT" and not matched:
153	                joined.append(left + (None,) * len(join.range.table.columns))
154	        rows = joined
155	    return rows
156	
157	
158	def _aggregate(expression: BoundExpr, values: list):
159	    if expression.value == "COUNT":
160	        return len(values) if not expression.children else sum(value is not None for value in values)
161	    non_null = [value for value in values if value is not None]
162	    if not non_null:
163	        return None
164	    if expression.value == "SUM":
165	        return sum(non_null)
166	    if expression.value == "AVG":
167	        return sum(non_null) / len(non_null)
168	    if expression.value == "MIN":
169	        return min(non_null)
170	    return max(non_null)

1	"""R1 static runtime audit; tests may use pytest, minisql itself may not.
2	
3	Python >=3.10 supplies sys.stdlib_module_names. On the available 3.9 host,
4	use the interpreter's configured stdlib/platstdlib and lib-dynload directories
5	plus builtin names, never sys.path or site-packages. The fallback is not a
6	claim that Python 3.9 meets the product's >=3.11 runtime requirement.
7	"""
8	
9	import ast
10	import importlib.machinery
11	from pathlib import Path
12	import pkgutil
13	import sys
14	import sysconfig
15	
16	import pytest
17	
18	
19	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
20	PACKAGE = ROOT / "minisql"
21	FORBIDDEN = {"sqlite3", "_sqlite3", "sqlparse", "sqlglot", "duckdb", "sqlalchemy",
22	             "pglast", "moz_sql_parser", "sql_metadata", "pyparsing", "lark"}
23	
24	
25	def stdlib_names():
26	    if hasattr(sys, "stdlib_module_names"):
27	        return set(sys.stdlib_module_names)
28	    names = set(sys.builtin_module_names)
29	    directories = set()
30	    for key in ("stdlib", "platstdlib"):
31	        directory = Path(sysconfig.get_path(key))
32	        directories.add(directory)
33	        directories.add(directory / "lib-dynload")
34	    for directory in directories:
35	        if directory.is_dir():
36	            names.update(module.name for module in pkgutil.iter_modules([str(directory)]))
37	    return names - {"site-packages", "dist-packages"}
38	
39	
40	def import_targets(tree):
41	    """Yield static imports, including literal dynamic-import calls.
42	
43	    Unresolvable dynamic imports fail the audit rather than silently passing.
44	    Relative imports are checked against the on-disk package separately.
45	    """
46	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
47	        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
48	            for alias in node.names:
49	                yield alias.name, 0, node.lineno
50	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
51	            yield node.module or "", node.level, node.lineno
52	        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
53	            function = node.func
54	            dynamic = (isinstance(function, ast.Name) and function.id == "__import__") or (
55	                isinstance(function, ast.Attribute) and function.attr == "import_module")
56	            if dynamic:
57	                assert node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(
58	                    node.args[0].value, str), "nonliteral dynamic import cannot be statically audited"
59	                name = node.args[0].value
60	                yield name.lstrip("."), len(name) - len(name.lstrip(".")), node.lineno
61	
62	
63	def local_module_exists(parts):
64	    path = ROOT.joinpath(*parts)
65	    return path.with_suffix(".py").is_file() or (path / "__init__.py").is_file()
66	
67	
68	def audit_source(source, path, allowed):
69	    tree = ast.parse(source, filename=str(path))
70	    compile(tree, str(path), "exec")
71	    for name, level, line in import_targets(tree):
72	        first = name.split(".")[0]
73	        assert first not in FORBIDDEN, "{}:{} forbidden SQL/parser import {}".format(path, line, name)
74	        if level:
75	            relative_parent = path.relative_to(ROOT).parent.parts
76	            assert level <= len(relative_parent), "relative import escapes runtime package"
77	            base = relative_parent[:len(relative_parent) - level + 1]
78	            parts = base + tuple(name.split(".")) if name else base
79	            assert local_module_exists(parts), "{}:{} missing local module {}".format(path, line, name)
80	        elif first == "minisql":
81	            assert local_module_exists(tuple(name.split("."))), "missing package module " + name
82	        else:
83	            assert first in allowed, "{}:{} non-stdlib import {}".format(path, line, name)
84	    return tree

32	def error_is(db, sql, cls, message, token, occurrence=1):
33	    # Locate the expected contract token independently, never from an engine AST.
34	    index = -1
35	    for _ in range(occurrence):
36	        index = sql.index(token, index + 1)
37	    line = sql.count("\n", 0, index) + 1
38	    previous_lf = sql.rfind("\n", 0, index)
39	    column = index - previous_lf
40	    kinds = {minisql.SemanticError: "Semantic", minisql.QueryRuntimeError: "Runtime",
41	             minisql.LexError: "Lex", minisql.ParseError: "Parse"}
42	    with pytest.raises(cls) as caught:
43	        db.execute(sql)
44	    error = caught.value
45	    assert type(error) is cls
46	    assert (error.kind, error.message, error.line, error.column) == (
47	        kinds[cls], message, line, column)
48	    assert str(error) == "{}Error at line {}, column {}: {}".format(kinds[cls], line, column, message)
